title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for history of colon cancer.

HPI: The patient is a 62-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up regarding his history of colon cancer. He underwent surgical resection and subsequent treatment several years ago. He reports feeling well and notes that he has experienced no new symptoms, such as changes in bowel habits, abdominal pain, or unexplained weight loss. He states that his primary treatment is complete and he has not had any issues since his last surveillance appointment. He is here today for a clinical evaluation and to review his current status.

Medication List:
- Multivitamin daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily

Review of Systems:
The patient denies any gastrointestinal distress, fever, chills, or night sweats. He denies any new-onset pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath. He reports no changes in appetite or energy levels.

Social History: The patient is a retired engineer. He lives with his wife and two children. He enjoys gardening and walking. He denies current tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History: Father had a history of hypertension. Mother had a history of type 2 diabetes. No known family history of colorectal malignancies.

Vitals:
Blood Pressure: 128/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Temperature: 98.6 F
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
SpO2: 98% on room air
Weight: 195 lbs
Height: 5'11"

Recent Labs:
Hemoglobin: 14.2 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.5 x 10^9/L
Platelets: 210 x 10^9/L
eGFR: 88 mL/min/1.73m2

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3. In no acute distress.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, and non-distended. Normal bowel sounds present. No palpable masses or organomegaly.
Skin: No suspicious lesions or changes noted.

Assessment:
The patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of colon cancer. The primary carcinoma was removed and treated years ago. He currently shows no evidence of recurrence at the primary site. There is no evidence of disease in other areas of the body. He remains asymptomatic and stable.

Plan:
1. Continue current surveillance schedule.
2. Maintain current medications.
3. Follow up in 6 months for next scheduled evaluation.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: The colon cancer was excised or eradicated, no treatment is directed to it and there is no evidence of it: personal history Z85.038 (no HCC). Any metastasis is still coded as a current secondary malignancy.

distractors.why: Treatment ended and there is no evidence of the primary: code personal history (Z85), not active cancer.
